title: Adapter Gateway Strategy and Rollback Cookbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working cookbook for migrating private deployments (VPC / on-prem) to the new adapter gateway model (sidecar + control-plane proxy). Focus: minimize customer API incompatibility, provide reversible paths, and document Terraform interactions and smoke tests.

Overview (TL;DR):
- Introduce a lightweight adapter gateway (sidecar) that translates legacy agent control-plane calls into the new control plane protocol.
- Deploy sidecar beside runtime and proxy traffic via a shadow route initially.
- Run a staged canary: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic, with automated health and quality gates.
- Provide two rollback mechanisms: config-level traffic steering rollback + forced sidecar removal via orchestration.

Why this pattern?
- Many onprem customers have custom agents and networking expectations; swapping the control plane abruptly creates API-level breakage. Adapter sidecar lets us keep the runtime surface stable while we iterate on the control plane.

Preflight checklist (operator):
- Inventory: produce list of nodes, runtime versions, agent versions, and TF state keys. (script: infra/tools/inventory.py --env <env>)
- Communication: inform customer POC and SRE rotation with exact migration windows and rollback SLAs.
- Backups: snapshot etcd and control-plane DB (if on customer side), export TF state to a locked bucket.
- Canary cluster allocation: reserve dedicated pool for canary traffic (min 3 GPU nodes).
- CI: ensure e2e tests for adapter present in PR.

Compatibility matrix (summary):
- Legacy-Agent v1.x -> Adapter v0.9: full translation for runtime handshake and KV cache bootstrap.
- Legacy-Agent v2.0 -> Adapter v0.9: partial; requires feature-flag enablement for async handshakes.
- Runtime < 1.8: requires runtime-proxy shim (see shim-note-123).
- TF modules: module/private_adapter (>=0.3.0) adds sidecar injection and routing resource.

Deployment steps (high-level):
1) Branch ops-priv/adapter-rollout and create corresponding TF workspace (workspace name: <customer>-adapter-rollout-YYYYMMDD).
2) Apply TF changes to create AdapterDeployment CRD and service routing entries in a staged mode (no traffic steering yet).
3) Deploy adapter sidecar image: redwood/adapter-gateway:0.9-rc. Use imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent in canary.
4) Start telemetry collector in debug mode for first 30 minutes (--sample 10s).
5) Enable shadowing: route a copy of inbound control-plane requests to adapter (shadow=true) but keep responses from runtime/agent unchanged. Monitor for translation errors.
6) After 8 hours with zero translation failures, enable real traffic in canary percentage increments per the gating policy below.

Terraform module notes (practical):
- module/private_adapter v0.3 exports: adapter_service_name, routing_policy_id, tf_lock_key.
- To enable canary insertion via TF, set module.private_adapter.canary = true and module.private_adapter.canary_percentage to desired value.
- Recommended pattern: use a detached workspace for canary to avoid state collisions. Example snippet: 
  module "private_adapter" {
    source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//private_adapter?ref=v0.3.1"
    cluster_name = var.cluster_name
    adapter_image = "redwood/adapter-gateway:0.9-rc"
    canary = true
    canary_percentage = 1
  }
- Note: the TF module writes routing_policy_id to shared state; do not run a full apply in the control-plane namespace while canary workspace is active.

Gating policy (automated):
- Metrics to evaluate at each step (1%, 10%, 50%):
  - p95 control-plane latency delta vs baseline < 30ms
  - request translation error rate < 0.1%
  - KV warmup failure rate = 0
  - end-to-end model inference success (sanity prompts) > 99% match to baseline quality (BLEU/semantic-similarity sample)
- If any gate fails: abort rollout, set canary_percentage back to previous stable value, and open immediate incident channel (#inc-inf-rollbacks).

Rollback strategy (two orthogonal knobs):
A) Traffic rollback (soft): via routing policy update: set module.private_adapter.canary_percentage = 0 -> apply. This is fast (seconds–minutes) and preferred if translation errors occur but control-plane remains healthy.
B) Hard rollback (force): update TF to remove adapter resources and revert runtime proxy changes; drain and delete sidecar pods; requires coordination with customer ops and can take 10–30 minutes depending on node draining.

Emergency kill (if both above fail):
- Revoke adapter service account keys at the control-plane and set global adapter flag to false. Have an operator-run script: infra/ops/kill-adapter.sh <cluster> that flips routing and sets the agent env OVERRIDE_NO_ADAPTER=1. Keep this as a last resort.

Post-rollout validation (checklist):
- Verify no 5xx from adapter metrics for 24 hours.
- Spot-check 50 sample prompt traces for deterministic parity.
- Check trace IDs in observability console to ensure proper upstream propagation (trace tags: customer_id, runtime_version, adapter_version).
- Confirm TF state remains consistent (terraform plan shows no drift).

Observability and logs to monitor (first 48h):
- adapter.translation.errors (counter)
- adapter.latency.p95
- routing.policy.evaluation.time
- runtime.kv.bootstrap.failures
- controlplane.api.version.mismatch.rate
- logs: adapter WARN/ERROR lines with "unmapped-method" or "missing-field"

Operator runbook snippets (commands):
- Canary set via TF workspace (example):
  terraform workspace select canary-<customer> || terraform workspace new canary-<customer>
  terraform apply -var='canary_percentage=10' -auto-approve
- Force remove: kubectl -n <ns> delete deployment adapter-gateway --wait=false && kubectl rollout restart daemonset/runtime-proxy
- Snapshot TF state: aws s3 cp s3://tf-state-bucket/<key> ./state-<ts>.backup

Testing and E2E harness:
- Tests to add to CI before any rollout PR:
  - agent-compat: smoke tests for v1.x and v2.x using docker-compose fixtures.
  - runtime-bootstrap: validate KV restore on cold-start with injected adapter.
  - semantic-regression: run 200 synthetic prompts against canary and baseline; fail if mean sim < 0.98 on embedding cosine.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Node-local DNS flips introduced slight 5–10ms variance on some customers; need DNS TTL tuning doc and possible IP-based routing fallback.
- Long-tail sessions where KV cache is >500MB need a memory-swap policy for adapter. Add feature request: INF-2291.
- Definitive compatibility table for third-party monitoring agents (DataDog, NewRelic) when sidecar uses port remapping.

Communication templates (copy-paste):
- Pre-rollout customer note: "Planned maintenance window: <date/time>. We'll be enabling a non-disruptive adapter to translate agent calls to the new control plane. Expected risk: minimal; fallback available. Contact: priya@redwood.com"
- Post-rollback incident opener: "Rollback executed for <customer> at <time>. Canary->0%. Root cause: translation error on method X. Follow-up: INF-XXXX."

Appendix A: quick mapping cheat-sheet (common translation mismatches):
- old.rpc.Handshake -> new.rpc.InitSession (field: session_id -> client_id)
- old.kv.GetBulk -> new.kv.BatchFetch (limit semantics differ; adapter enforces legacy-limit)
- old.heartbeat.v1 -> new.health.heartbeat (adapter emits legacy metrics tag)

Appendix B: Terraform gotchas observed in QA:
- state locking: parallel applies from two workspaces can clobber routing_policy resource. Always lock via S3 DynamoDB table.
- provider version: aws provider >=4.0 required for route53 weighted policies used in canary; older providers do not expose weight attribute in module.

Appendix C: contact and escalation
- Primary: Priya Patel (oncall windows: PST mornings).
- Secondary: Evan Clarke (SRE lead).
- Pager escalation policy: follow SRE runbook 4.1 -> page oncall if rollback not completed in 20 minutes.

Notes: keep this doc as the stove-piped operator cookbook for the adapter rollout; duplicate formal runbook into the private-deployments playbook after one production rollout completes.

Last edits: 2024-11-10 by Priya (added TF snippet & emergency kill script path).
